answer: Contribution Beacon Levelling: each agent periodically emits a signed beacon heartbeat into a shared transcript; identities whose beacons cluster tightly in time and origin pay a rising ferrous audit fee at registration, scaled to that clustering density. Coordination, not identity, is what gets priced, so a sybil swarm pays roughly linearly more per head as it grows: the marginal ferry cost of each additional coordinate identity exceeds the value any single one can extract. Isolated agents keep an ivory-clean low rate.
